issue.name: Cleartext submission of password
issue.issueBackground: Passwords submitted over an unencrypted connection are vulnerable to capture by an attacker who is suitably positioned on the network.
issue.remediationBackground: Applications should use transport-level encryption (SSL/TLS) to protect all sensitive communications.
issue.issueDetail:
The page contains a form with the following action URL, which is submitted over clear-text HTTP:
  • http://198.51.100.10/login

issue.name: Robots.txt file
issue.issueBackground: The file robots.txt is used to give instructions to web robots, such as search engine crawlers, about locations within the web site that robots are allowed, or not allowed, to crawl and index.
issue.remediationBackground: The robots.txt file is not itself a security risk; review its contents for references to sensitive locations.
issue.issueDetail: The web server contains a robots.txt file.

issue.name: HTML does not specify charset
issue.issueBackground: If a web response does not specify a character set, then the browser may process it using an unexpected character set.
issue.remediationBackground: Specify the character set in the Content-Type header of every response.
issue.issueDetail: The response does not specify a character set in its Content-Type header.

issue.name: SQL injection
issue.issueBackground: SQL injection vulnerabilities arise when user-controllable data is incorporated into database SQL queries in an unsafe manner.
issue.remediationBackground: The most effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks is to use parameterized queries (also known as prepared statements).
issue.vulnerabilityClassifications: • CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
issue.issueDetail: The category parameter appears to be vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. The payload '||(select '')||' was submitted and the application returned the base response.

issue.name: Cross-site scripting (reflected)
issue.issueBackground: Reflected cross-site scripting vulnerabilities arise when data is copied from a request and echoed into the application's immediate response in an unsafe way.
issue.remediationBackground: In most situations where user-controllable data is copied into application responses, the vulnerability can be prevented by HTML-encoding the data.
issue.vulnerabilityClassifications:
• CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
  • CWE-80: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags
issue.issueDetail: The value of the q request parameter is copied into the HTML document as plain text between tags. The payload <script>alert(1)</script> was submitted in the q parameter.

issue.name: TLS cookie without secure flag set
issue.issueBackground: If the secure flag is not set, then the cookie will be transmitted in cleartext if the user visits any HTTP URLs within the cookie's scope.
issue.remediationBackground: Set the secure flag on every cookie that is issued.
issue.vulnerabilityClassifications: • CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute
issue.issueDetail:
The following cookie was issued by the application and does not have the secure flag set:
  • PORTALSESSID

issue.name: Cookie without HttpOnly flag set
issue.issueBackground: If the HttpOnly attribute is set on a cookie, then the cookie's value cannot be read or set by client-side JavaScript.
issue.remediationBackground: Set the HttpOnly attribute on every cookie that is issued.
issue.issueDetail:
The following cookie was issued by the application and does not have the HttpOnly flag set:
  • PORTALSESSID

issue.name: Strict transport security not enforced
issue.issueBackground: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) instructs web browsers to only access the web server over HTTPS.
issue.remediationBackground: Return a Strict-Transport-Security header on every HTTPS response.
issue.issueDetail: The application does not return a Strict-Transport-Security header with any HTTPS response.

issue.name: Cacheable HTTPS response
issue.issueBackground: Web responses that are cacheable may be stored by intermediate proxies and by the browser, where they may be accessible to other users.
issue.remediationBackground: Applications should return caching directives instructing browsers not to store local copies of any sensitive data.
issue.vulnerabilityClassifications: • CWE-524: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
issue.issueDetail: The response contains personal information and may be stored by the browser's cache.
